  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The positive case of `test_support_checkout_job_wrapper_sources_only_the_verified_checkout` plants the step script at line 320 before `_commit_support_checkout()` runs, and that function stages only `README`, so the wrapper sources an untracked file and the test never proves the script's contents come from the commit `WORKFLOW_SUPPORT_REF` points to.
  WHY: The test checks only that HEAD matches and that the file exists, so it would not catch a wrapper regression that accepts untracked content or drops the rev-parse check; this is a test-fidelity gap, not a production defect. Three reviewers rated it NIT (mapped to low) and google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite gave no severity. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly dropped this item as having no runtime failure path.

- requirement: "A workflow that comes within 30,000 bytes of the 430,000-byte test ceiling opens a `ai:ci-budget` issue before any test fails."
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `jobs.budget-watch` trigger or condition
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `budget-watch` remains restricted to pushes to `main` at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:5095-5101`, full final CI runs through `workflow_dispatch` against the PR merge ref (lines 22-28), the PR changes the warning threshold fallback at line 5129 but does not make the watcher run for that final CI, so a PR that raises a workflow from below 400,000 bytes to at least 430,000 bytes skips the watcher while its size test fails. Both reviewers rated it MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash each rejected this gap as out of scope: the issue's "Automation and wiring" section names the existing `budget-watch` job as the entry point and forbids new jobs (§33).

  PROBLEM: The positive test for verified script sourcing plants an untracked script at the expected location and confirms it is sourced.
  WHY: The test does not verify that the sourced script contents actually originate from the commit SHA identified by WORKFLOW_SUPPORT_REF; it only verifies that sourcing an existing file works, which can lead to false positives if the wrong script is in the workspace.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: A workflow that comes within 30,000 bytes of the 430,000-byte test ceiling opens an ai:ci-budget issue before any test fails.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml, jobs.budget-watch trigger or condition.
  Evidence of absence: budget-watch remains restricted to github.event_name == 'push' on refs/heads/main. PR final CI runs via workflow_dispatch on the PR merge ref, so a PR that raises a workflow from below 400,000 bytes to at least 430,000 bytes skips the watcher while its size test fails.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_review_autofix_step_fallback_verify.py:281-335 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In `test_support_checkout_job_wrapper_sources_only_the_verified_checkout`, the `_plant` call plants an untracked script at line 320, before `_commit_support_checkout` at line 328 commits only README. The file therefore exists in the working directory but is not part of the verified commit, and the wrapper checks only `git rev-parse HEAD == ${WORKFLOW_SUPPORT_REF}`.
  WHY: The test is weaker than the property it claims to verify. If `.codex-workflow-src/scripts/<script>` were ever populated by something other than `actions/checkout`, the wrapper would still source it and the test would not catch that. The existing `test_wrapper_keeps_verified_fallback_and_staged_bundle` has the same weakness, so this test inherits it. The new test should commit the planted script.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- tests/test_review_autofix_step_fallback_verify.py:`_commit_support_checkout()` lines 81–88; test lines 320 and 328–336 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The positive test plants the step script before creating the support commit, but `_commit_support_checkout()` stages only `README`, and the test expects the wrapper to source that untracked script when `WORKFLOW_SUPPORT_REF` matches the commit.
  WHY: The test passes without proving the sourced script belongs to the pinned commit; a wrapper that accepts untracked script content would still pass, leaving that fallback behavior unverified.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: “A workflow that comes within 30,000 bytes of the 430,000-byte test ceiling opens a `ai:ci-budget` issue before any test fails.”
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `jobs.budget-watch` trigger or condition.
  Evidence of absence: `budget-watch` remains restricted to pushes to `main` at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:5095-5101`. The workflow documents that full final CI runs through `workflow_dispatch` against the PR merge ref at lines 22-28. The PR changes the warning threshold fallback at line 5129, but does not make the watcher run for that final CI. Therefore, a PR that crosses the test ceiling can fail its size test before the watcher opens an issue.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- tests/test_review_autofix_step_fallback_verify.py:`_commit_support_checkout` (lines 81-88, commits only `README`) vs `test_support_checkout_job_wrapper_sources_only_the_verified_checkout` (lines 312-336, added in LAST RUN DIFF) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The positive case (lines 333-336) plants `scripts/<script>` into `.codex-workflow-src` (line 320) via `_plant` and then commits only `README`. It expects the wrapper to source the untracked script once `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `WORKFLOW_SUPPORT_REF`, so it proves HEAD equality plus file existence but never that the script's contents belong to the verified commit.
  WHY: Test-only. The test cannot catch a regression that relaxes the wrapper's HEAD check into a plain file-existence check (or drops rev-parse for the `[ ! -f ]` term only). It mirrors the wrapper's own contract (HEAD + existence; `actions/checkout` guarantees committed content), so this is a test-fidelity gap, not a production defect.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
